Subject: Transfer impact assessment request — Emerald (HIPAA, SCCs, DPIA)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams have a couple of follow-ups before we can proceed to procurement: specifically a Transfer Impact Assessment covering EU->US processing of patient pseudonymized data and evidence of controls for HIPAA-like obligations. Can you share a concise TIA summary (high-level routing, subprocessors, SCCs status) and the specific artifacts we can put in our DPIA evidence pack?

Key asks:
- Can you confirm whether traffic can be restricted to eu-central-1 and whether Redwood will sign SCCs?
- Evidence: SOC 2 report, SCC execution note, network architecture (EU region), key management details, and any pseudonymization guidance.
- Timeline: we need this by EOD Friday if possible to keep our procurement timeline.

Attaching our vendor questionnaire snapshot (we'll send the full SIG separately).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Data Governance
Emerald Health Systems

If you need the vendor SIG, ask and we'll prioritize. If Friday EOD is strict, we should be able to get the bundle ready — otherwise propose a 30-min call tomorrow to align.

Eve / team — technical notes for the bundle:

1) Routing/Regions: Redwood supports region pinning. For Emerald we can configure all inference and KV caches to eu-central-1 (aws eu-central-1) and ensure ingress/egress stays in-region for model execution. In hosted mode we route requests by policy; private/dedicated modes allow strict region isolation.

2) Subprocessors: list included in the attached EU-US_SCCs-execution-note.pdf — includes cloud provider, monitoring, and logging partners.

3) Encryption & KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for Private and Dedicated customers, and our hosted offering uses compartmentalized keys with AES-256 at rest + TLS1.3 in transit. We'll include key rotation cadence and HSM-backed KMS options.

4) Pseudonymization: recommended pattern is minimal PI in prompts, tokenization at ingestion, and KV cache TTLs set to short windows. We provide a pseudonymization guidance doc (excerpt in the TIA PDF).

5) Attachments I produced: redwood-eu-network-arch.png (diagram), EU-US_SCCs-execution-note.pdf.

I also flagged a few items that Legal may want to redline in the DPA — noted in comments in the execution note.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect

Attachments: redwood-eu-network-arch.png, EU-US_SCCs-execution-note.pdf

From: Legal Ops <legal.ops@emeraldhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@emeraldhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 15:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Transfer impact assessment request — Emerald (HIPAA, SCCs, DPIA)

Evelyn — thanks for the quick turn. A couple of clarifying items from Legal:

- We need confirmation that logs containing user identifiers are not exported outside EU-maintained projects by default (we can accept export only for security incidents with approval). Can you confirm log partitioning?
- For HIPAA alignment: can you provide a short statement on whether PHI is stored at rest in identifiable form, and if so what pseudonymization measures exist and sample retention TTLs?
- SCCs: we require an executed SCC or an SOC2+SCCs addendum. If you cannot provide a fully executed SCC before contract signature, please confirm an expected execution timeline.

We prefer documentation in a shared Drive link. Also, can you indicate whether you support a contractual Audit Window (e.g., once per year) and whether you have an on-premise/private deployment option for air-gapped work?

Thanks — Tom (Legal Ops)

Tom/Sofia — short answers and next steps below. We produced a compact bundle and upload it to your shared drive link; links and files attached.

Quick responses:
- Log partitioning: by default we partition telemetry and access logs at the account/project level. Logs are retained in EU storage for customers who opt for EU-only routing; export outside EU requires an explicit Ops request and approval workflow. We'll include a sample retention configuration (in DPIA-evidence-matrix.xlsx).
- PHI at rest: Redwood does not require storing identifiable PHI for inference. Where customers choose to persist de-identified or pseudonymized artifacts, the recommended pattern is per-customer tokenization with short TTLs (configurable). We included a short pseudonymization statement in the TIA summary.
- SCCs: Redwood will execute SCCs; for Emerald we can provide an SCC addendum signature timeline of two weeks from countersignature of the DPA. We included EU-US_SCCs-execution-note.pdf for detail.
- Audit window / on-prem: We support annual audit windows for Dedicated/Private plans and have an on-prem/private deployment package for regulated customers — details in the attached DPA excerpt.

Attachments & links included in the shared bundle:
- Redwood_TIA_summary_for_Emerald_20270303.pdf (one-page TIA summary)
- DPIA-evidence-matrix.xlsx (artifact checklist and sample snippets)
- EU-US_SCCs-execution-note.pdf (subprocessor list + SCC timeline)
- redwood-eu-network-arch.png (diagram)

- Dev: prepare redacted SOC 2 and guidance on KMS rotation for inclusion.
- Emerald: confirm whether you will require an on-prem evaluation or if Dedicated (EU-only) is acceptable.

If helpful, I've created a HubSpot deal and a DocuSign envelope for the SCCs (links above).
